items.stem: Select from the following a decomposition reaction in which the source of energy for decomposition is light:

options.label: A
options.text: 2FeSO₄ → Fe₂O₃ + SO₂ + SO₃

options.label: B
options.text: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂

options.label: C
options.text: 2AgBr → 2Ag + Br₂

options.label: D
options.text: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂

items.answer: 2AgBr → 2Ag + Br₂. Silver bromide decomposes in sunlight, so light is the source of energy. A reaction in which a single substance breaks down to form two or more substances is a decomposition reaction.

items.stem: MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + 2H₂O + Cl₂. The reaction given above is a redox reaction because in this case

options.label: B
options.text: HCl is oxidised

options.label: C
options.text: MnO₂ is reduced

options.label: D

items.answer: MnO₂ is reduced and HCl is oxidised. In the reaction MnO₂ loses oxygen (reduction) and HCl loses hydrogen (oxidation).

items.stem: Consider the following chemical equations I and II. I. Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂  II. NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O. The correct statement about these equations is:

options.label: A
options.text: ‘I’ is a displacement reaction and ‘II’ is a decomposition reaction.

options.label: B
options.text: ‘I’ is a displacement reaction and ‘II’ is a double displacement reaction.

options.label: C
options.text: Both ‘I’ and ‘II’ are displacement reactions.

options.label: D
options.text: Both ‘I’ and ‘II’ are double-displacement reactions.

items.answer: Equation I is a displacement reaction - Mg displaces hydrogen from HCl. Equation II is a double displacement reaction because the ions of both reactants exchange places to form two different compounds.

(i) In beakers A and B, an exothermic process has occurred. (ii) In beakers A and B, an endothermic process has occurred. (iii) In beaker C an exothermic process has occurred. options.label: C

items.answer: (i) and (iv). A rise in temperature means heat is released, which is exothermic; a fall in temperature means heat is absorbed, which is endothermic.

items.stem: A solution of potassium chloride when mixed with silver nitrate solution forms an insoluble white substance. Write the chemical reaction involved and also mention the type of the chemical reaction.
items.answer: KCl(aq) + AgNO₃(aq) → AgCl(s) + KNO₃(aq). It is a double displacement reaction and also a precipitation reaction, because the insoluble white silver chloride is precipitated.

items.stem: Ferrous sulphate decomposes with the evolution of a gas having the characteristic odour of burning sulphur. Write the chemical reaction involved and identify the type of reaction.
items.answer: 2FeSO₄(s) →(heat) Fe₂O₃(s) + SO₂(g) + SO₃(g). It is a thermal decomposition reaction.

items.stem: Why do fireflies glow at night?
items.answer: Fireflies undergo a process known as bioluminescence. They contain phosphorus compounds which give out heat and light from their body.

items.stem: Grapes hanging on the plant do not ferment but after being plucked from the plant can be fermented. Under what conditions do these grapes ferment? Is it a chemical or a physical change?
items.answer: Fermentation of grapes takes place under anaerobic conditions, that is in the absence of air. New products are formed, so it is a chemical change.

items.stem: Which among the following are physical or chemical changes? (a) Evaporation of petrol (b) Burning of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) (c) Heating of an iron rod to red hot (d) Curdling of milk (e) Sublimation of solid ammonium chloride
items.answer: (a), (c) and (e) are physical changes. (b) and (d) are chemical changes.

items.stem: Explain electrolytic decomposition with suitable examples.
items.answer:
When electricity is passed through a molten compound which is ionic in nature, then the ions of the compound separate into components, decomposing the compound. Example:
2H₂O(l) —Electricity→ 2H₂(g) + O₂(g)
This is an example of electrolytic decomposition since a compound is decomposed by passing electricity through it.

items.stem: When ferrous sulphate is heated, the green colour of ferrous sulphate changes to brown due to the formation of ferric oxide, with a smell of burning sulphur. Explain the reaction.
items.answer:
The given reaction can be represented as:
2FeSO₄ → Fe₂O₃ + SO₂↑ + SO₃↑
(ferrous sulphate, green) → (ferric oxide, brown) + sulphur dioxide + sulphur trioxide
Since ferrous sulphate is decomposed, on heating, into ferric oxide, sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide, this is a thermal decomposition reaction.

items.stem:
Consider the following displacement reactions:
(i) CuSO₄(aq) + Fe(s) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu(s)
(ii) FeSO₄(aq) + Zn(s) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Fe(s)
State which is the most reactive and which is the least reactive metal out of zinc, copper and iron.
items.answer:
(i) In the first reaction, iron displaces Cu from CuSO₄ solution, so iron is more reactive than copper.
(ii) In the second reaction, zinc displaces iron from its sulphate solution, so zinc is more reactive than iron.
Thus, zinc is more reactive than iron which is more reactive than copper. Therefore zinc is the most reactive and copper is the least reactive metal.

items.stem: What are oxidation reactions?
items.answer:
It is a process in which (a) oxygen or any electronegative element is added up, or (b) hydrogen or any electropositive element is removed, or (c) electrons are released. Examples are:
(a) Sulphur burns in air with a blue flame to form sulphur dioxide. Oxygen is added to sulphur.
S(s) + O₂(g) → SO₂(g)  (addition of oxygen to sulphur)
(b) Hydrogen sulphide combines with iodine to give hydrogen iodide and sulphur.
H₂S + I₂ → 2HI + S  (removal of hydrogen from H₂S)
(c) Sodium atom ionises to give Na⁺ ions.
Na → Na⁺ + e⁻  (release of electron)

items.stem: What does a balanced chemical equation convey?
items.answer:
A balanced chemical equation conveys the following information:
(i) Formulae of the substances taking part in the chemical reaction, i.e. the reactants.
(ii) Formulae of the substances produced in the reaction, i.e. the products.
(iii) The relative number of molecules of reactants and products.
(iv) The relative masses of reactants and products.
(v) The relative volumes of the gaseous substances involved in the reaction.

C(graphite) + 2H₂(g) → CH₄(g)   ΔH = +74.25 kJ

items.stem: Give chemical explanation for evolution and absorption of heat in a chemical reaction.
items.answer:
Atoms in the molecule of an element or a compound are held together by chemical bonds. During a chemical reaction, bonds between the atoms of the reactants are broken and new bonds are formed between the atoms of the products. When bonds are broken, energy is absorbed, and when new bonds are formed, energy is released.
(i) If the energy released during the formation of new bonds is more than the energy used up in breaking the old bonds, the overall reaction will be exothermic (heat is evolved).
(ii) If the energy released during the formation of new bonds is less than the energy required to break the bonds, the overall reaction will be endothermic (heat is absorbed).

items.stem: How is a chemical equation written? Illustrate with an example.
items.answer:
Let it be required to write a chemical equation that describes the reaction between magnesium and sulphuric acid to produce magnesium sulphate and hydrogen.

(ii) Separate the reacting substances from the products by a symbol meaning "produce". The sign → (an arrow), or sometimes the sign =, is used for this purpose.

(iii) Then put a + sign between the reactants indicating that these 'react', and a + sign between the products which signifies 'and'.

items.stem: Describe the method of balancing a chemical equation.
items.answer:
The following sequential steps should be taken to obtain a balanced chemical equation: (i) First the skeleton equation is written. For example, H₂ + O₂ → H₂O (ii) The same total of charges should appear on the left and right side of the equation. (iii) Now one of the atoms is made equal on both sides by multiplying a molecule or compound with an integral number so that the desired element is balanced. It is convenient to start with the molecule or compound that contains the maximum number of atoms. Here, H₂O contains the maximum number of atoms. It is one short of an oxygen atom and so it is multiplied by 2: H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O (iv) Next, the effect of multiplication of the molecule on the balance of other atoms is examined. As is seen, the number of oxygen atoms on both sides balances but now the number of hydrogen atoms on the left is 2 less. So, multiply H₂ on the left by 2: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O (v) Further, count the number of atoms of each type on both sides.
AtomOn rightOn left
H44
022
Now, the equation is balanced. If the number of atoms on both sides do not agree, the above steps should be continued till a balanced equation is obtained. This is called the hit and trial method. If the reaction is complicated, i.e., it involves a large number of reactants and products, it is preferred to write the equation in steps (the actual reaction may or may not take place in these steps). For example, when copper reacts with conc. nitric acid, the products are copper nitrate, nitrogen dioxide and water. Cu + HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + NO₂ + H₂O We can write this reaction in three steps and balance each step separately. (i) First, HNO₃ is decomposed to give nitrogen dioxide (NO₂), water (H₂O) and atomic oxygen. 2HNO₃ → 2NO₂ + H₂O + O ...(1) (ii) In the next step, copper is oxidised to copper(II) oxide (CuO). Cu + O → CuO ...(2) (iii) Copper oxide so formed then reacts with nitric acid to form copper nitrate, Cu(NO₃)₂, and water. CuO + 2HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + H₂O ...(3) Next, eq. (1), (2), (3) are multiplied by an integer so that on adding (1), (2) and (3), the intermediate products (which do not appear in the final reaction) cancel out. In this case we find that the integer is one. So (1), (2) and (3) are added and the final balanced equation is written as below: Cu + 4HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO₂ + 2H₂O This method is known as the partial equation method.

items.stem: How can a chemical reaction be made more informative?

H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) → 2HCl(g)   ΔH = −184.7 kJ

items.stem: Define the terms: (i) Oxidising agent and (ii) Reducing agent.
items.answer:
(i) Oxidising agent: It is the substance which in a reaction (a) gives up oxygen or any electronegative element, or (b) accepts hydrogen or any electropositive element, or (c) accepts electrons.
(ii) Reducing agent: It is the substance which in a reaction (a) gives up hydrogen or any electropositive element, or (b) accepts oxygen or any electronegative element, or (c) releases electrons.
In the following reaction:
H₂S + Cl₂ → S + 2HCl
Chlorine accepts hydrogen from H₂S, thus oxidising it, and is called the oxidising agent.
In a chemical reaction, the oxidising agent is reduced and the reducing agent is oxidised. In the reaction between zinc and copper sulphate solution:
Zn + Cu²⁺SO₄²⁻ → Zn²⁺SO₄²⁻ + Cu
Zn reduces Cu²⁺ to Cu, itself being oxidised to Zn²⁺, so Zn acts as a reducing agent.

(ii) Type of reaction involved.
(iii) Is there any precipitate formed?
(iv) If any precipitate formed, write the colour of the precipitate.

(i) Na₂SO₄(aq) + BaCl₂(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq)

items.stem:
When a green salt is heated strongly, its colour finally changes to brown and the odour of burning sulphur is given out.
(a) Name the iron salt and write its formula.
(b) Name the brown substance obtained and write its formula.
(c) Which product gives the odour of burning sulphur? Write the formula.
(d) Write the chemical equation of the reaction involved.
(e) Name the type of chemical reaction which takes place during the heating of the iron salt.
items.answer:
(a) Ferrous sulphate, FeSO₄
(b) Ferric oxide, Fe₂O₃
(c) Sulphur dioxide, SO₂
(d) 2FeSO₄(s) --Heat--> Fe₂O₃(s) + SO₂(g) + SO₃(g)
    (ferrous sulphate → ferric oxide + sulphur dioxide + sulphur trioxide)

items.stem:
(a) Define corrosion.
(b) What is the name given to the corrosion of iron?
(c) What is the colour of the coating formed on silver and copper?
(d) What damage is caused by corrosion?
(e) How can we prevent corrosion?
items.answer:
(a) The surface of a metal reacts with atmospheric oxygen, moisture and carbon dioxide to form a coating on the surface. This phenomenon is called corrosion.
(b) When the metal involved is iron, the phenomenon of corrosion is called rusting.
(c) Silver forms a black coating and copper forms a green coating on the surface when exposed to the atmosphere for a long time.
(d) Corrosion weakens the metal. A great deal of damage is caused to car bodies, bridges, iron railings and ships.
(e) Corrosion can be prevented by coating the metal surface with paint.
items.ocr: The printed answer key omits the labels '(c)' and '(e)'; the sentence about the black and green coatings answers (c) and the closing sentence about painting answers (e), so the labels have been restored. 'When the metal involved in iron' read as 'is iron'.

items.stem:
(i) Name two effects of oxidation in daily life.
(ii) Why do iron articles become brown after some time?
(iii) Define the term corrosion. Give an example of corrosion.
(iv) Give the conditions of corrosion.
(v) What is rancidity?
items.answer:
(i) Corrosion and rancidity.
(ii) Due to corrosion (rusting of iron).
(iii) The process in which metals are eaten up gradually by the action of air, moisture or a chemical (such as an acid) on their surface is called corrosion. Example: the rusting of iron.
(iv) (a) Presence of moisture. (b) Presence of air (oxygen).
(v) Rancidity: When fats and oils are oxidised (or kept in the open for some days), their smell and taste change. We say that they have gone rancid. The condition produced by aerial oxidation of fats and oils in foods, marked by an unpleasant smell and taste, is called rancidity. Rancidity spoils food materials prepared in fats and oils which have been kept for a considerable time and makes them unfit for eating.
items.ocr: The printed question number was lost in extraction — this question runs straight on from Q247's answer with no number. It sits between Q247 and Q249, so it is numbered 248.

items.stem:
Identify the type of chemical reaction and write a balanced chemical equation for each of the following:
(a) Barium chloride solution is mixed with copper sulphate solution and a white precipitate is observed.
(b) On heating copper powder in a china dish, the surface of copper powder becomes black.
(c) On heating green ferrous sulphate crystals, a reddish brown solid is left and gases having the smell of burning sulphur are noticed.
(d) Iron nails when left dipped in blue copper sulphate solution become brownish in colour and the blue colour of copper sulphate solution turns to light green.
(e) Quicklime reacts vigorously with water releasing a large amount of heat.
items.answer:
(a) BaCl₂(aq) + CuSO₄(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + CuCl₂(aq) — Double displacement reaction.
(b) 2Cu(s) + O₂(g) --Heat--> 2CuO(s) — Oxidation-reduction reaction.
(c) 2FeSO₄(s) --Heat--> Fe₂O₃(s) + SO₂(g) + SO₃(g) — Decomposition reaction.
(d) Fe(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu(s) — Displacement reaction.
(e) CaO(s) + H₂O(l) → Ca(OH)₂ + Heat — Combination reaction.
items.ocr: Part (a) prints 'and while precipitate is observed'; read as 'a white precipitate'. The arrow in answer (c) was emitted with a stray dash ('--Heat--> -'); removed.

(a) Write a balanced chemical equation for the process of photosynthesis and the conditions of the reaction, giving physical states of all the substances.
(b) Classify the following chemical reactions as exothermic or endothermic:
(i) Electrolysis of water.
(ii) Burning of natural gas.
(iii) Decomposition of calcium carbonate.
(iv) Burning of magnesium ribbon in air.

(b) (i) Endothermic reaction.
(ii) Exothermic reaction.
(iii) Endothermic reaction.

items.stem:
A student prepared oxygen in a lab by catalytic decomposition of potassium chlorate (KClO₃) as shown in the figure. Decomposition of potassium chlorate gives potassium chloride (KCl) and oxygen (O₂). The following reaction takes place:
KClO₃(s) → KCl(s) + O₂(g)
(i) How many moles of KClO₃ are required to produce 2.4 moles of O₂?
(ii) Name the element which is reduced in the given reaction.
(iii) How many moles of KClO₃ give 3 moles of oxygen?
(iv) What is the oxidation state of chlorine in potassium chlorate?
items.answer:
(i) 3 moles of O₂ are formed by 2 moles of KClO₃, so 2.4 moles of O₂ will be formed by (2/3) × 2.4 = 1.6 moles of KClO₃.
(ii) Chlorine.
(iii) 2 moles of KClO₃ ≡ 3 moles of O₂.
(iv) The oxidation state of chlorine in potassium chlorate is +5.
items.ocr: NODIA math-mode artefacts repaired: '^KClO3h' → (KClO₃) and '^O $2$ h' → (O₂); the LaTeX equation was rewritten in Unicode with the → arrow restored. items.stem:
When two or more substances react and form some new substance, it is called a chemical reaction. Chemical equation is represented in terms of symbols, molecular formulas, moles, states, etc. As we know, all chemical reactions obey the law of chemical combination. Therefore, chemical reactions need to be balanced. It is done by hit and trial method. The chemical reactions can be classified into different types such as combination reaction, decomposition reaction, displacement reaction, double displacement reaction. The reactions that take place in solution are precipitation reactions and neutralisation reactions.
(i) Define a chemical equation.
(ii) Which law is followed by all chemical reactions?
(iii) Name four types of chemical reactions.
(iv) Give example of precipitation reactions.
items.answer:
(i) A chemical reaction is defined as the reaction in which two or more substances react to form a new substance.
(ii) The law of chemical combination is followed by all chemical reactions.
(iii) Combination reactions, displacement reactions, double displacement reactions and decomposition reactions are four types of chemical reactions.
(iv) The reaction between silver nitrate and sodium chloride that forms a precipitate of silver chloride and sodium nitrate is an example of a precipitation reaction.
items.ocr: The page-38 photograph printed with this case passage (a solution being poured into a beaker, a yellow precipitate forming) is attached, but the four parts can be answered without it, so figure_required is left false. Source defect: part (i) asks for a definition of a chemical EQUATION while the printed answer defines a chemical REACTION; the printed answer is kept as it stands. Printed answer (iv) repeats 'and sodium nitrate' twice — the duplicate was dropped. Passage grammar repaired ('all chemical reaction obeys', 'The reactions take place in solution is').

items.stem:
Corrosion is the phenomenon of deterioration of surface of metal in presence of air and moisture. It is a natural process and in the presence of a moist atmosphere, chemically active metals get corroded. This is an oxidation reaction. Rusting is the process where iron corrodes due to exposure to the atmosphere. The main circumstance of corrosion occurs with iron because it is a structural material in construction, bridges, buildings, rail transport, ships, etc. Aluminium is also an important structural metal, but even aluminium undergoes oxidation reactions. However, aluminium doesn't corrode or oxidize as rapidly as its reactivity suggests. An alloy of aluminium or any other metal like magnesium can make aluminium stronger and harder. Copper (Cu) corrodes and forms a basic green carbonate and lead corrodes to form a white lead oxide or carbonate.
(i) What is rusting?
(ii) Which two metals do not corrode easily?
(iii) List two properties of alloys.
(iv) What is the effect of corrosion on electrical conductivity?
items.answer:
(i) The deterioration of the surface of iron in presence of air and moisture is called rusting.
(ii) Gold and platinum.
(iii) (a) Alloys are more resistant to corrosion. (b) The melting point of alloys is less than that of pure metals.
(iv) Corrosion increases the electrical conductivity of metals.
items.ocr: OCR typos repaired in the passage and stem: 'Aluminium s also' → 'Aluminium is also', 'corresion' → 'corrosion'. Source defect: the printed answer (iv) states that corrosion INCREASES electrical conductivity, which is scientifically wrong — corrosion products are poor conductors, so corrosion lowers a metal's electrical conductivity. The printed answer is reproduced as it stands and the error flagged here.

items.stem:
Oxidation is the process of gaining of oxygen or losing of hydrogen. Reduction is the process of losing of oxygen or gaining of hydrogen. The substance which undergoes oxidation is the reducing agent while the substance which undergoes reduction is known as the oxidising agent. Oxidation and reduction always take place together and these types of reactions are known as redox reactions. Some of the examples of redox reactions are given below:
a. Pb₃O₄ + 8HCl → 3PbCl₂ + Cl₂ + 4H₂O
b. 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
c. CuSO₄ + Zn → Cu + ZnSO₄
d. V₂O₅ + 5Ca → 2V + 5CaO
e. 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂
f. CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O
(i) Give two examples of oxidation reaction from your everyday life.
(ii) Write the oxidising agent in the reaction a and b.
(iii) Out of oxidation and reduction, which reaction takes place at anode?
items.answer:
(i) (a) Corrosion (b) Rancidity
(ii) CuSO₄ and CuO
(iii) Oxidation takes place at the anode.
items.ocr: Reaction (a) printed '4H₂C' — restored to 4H₂O. Source defect: part (ii) asks for the oxidising agents of reactions (a) and (b), but the printed answer names CuSO₄ and CuO, which are the oxidising agents of reactions (c) and (f); the oxidising agents in (a) and (b) are Pb₃O₄ and O₂. The printed answer is reproduced as it stands and the mismatch flagged here. This case study prints only three parts, not four.

items.stem:
'Salts' refer to the compound formed when an acid reacts with a base. These reactions are known as neutralisation reactions. These reactions are often used in the laboratories to calculate the exact concentration of an acid or an alkali when the other is known. The familiar example of salt is sodium chloride (NaCl), which we use in our food on daily basis and is known as rock salt. It is prepared by the reaction of hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide solution. This salt is used to prepare various compounds. When electricity is passed through an aqueous solution of sodium chloride (called brine), it decomposes to form sodium hydroxide. The process is called the chlor-alkali process because of the products formed — 'chlor' for chlorine and 'alkali' for sodium hydroxide.
(i) Write the chemical reaction of chlor-alkali process.
(ii) Name the gases formed at the anode and the cathode.
(iii) Write one use each of chlorine and hydrogen gas.
(iv) How will you prepare baking soda from sodium chloride?
items.answer:
(i) 2NaCl + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + Cl₂ + H₂
(ii) Anode: chlorine gas; Cathode: hydrogen gas.
(iii) Chlorine is used to purify water. Hydrogen gas is used as a fuel.
(iv) When a cold and concentrated solution of sodium chloride reacts with ammonia and carbon dioxide, sodium hydrogencarbonate (baking soda) and ammonium chloride are formed:
NaCl + NH₃ + H₂O + CO₂ → NaHCO₃ (baking soda) + NH₄Cl
items.ocr: The page-39 membrane-cell diagram (labelled Anode+/−Cathode, Cl₂ and H₂ outlets, brine in and brine containing NaOH out) is printed between the passage and the parts and is what part (ii) reads the anode/cathode products off, so it is attached and required. Run-together OCR 'the products formedchlor and alkali for sodium hydroxide' restored to 'the products formed — chlor for chlorine and alkali for sodium hydroxide'; 'electricity is pass through' → 'is passed through'.

items.stem:
There are different types of chemical reactions occurring around us or being carried out for the benefit of mankind, e.g. combination reactions, decomposition reactions, displacement reactions, precipitation reactions, reduction-oxidation (redox) reactions, photochemical reactions etc. Now, answer the following questions:
(i) Combustion of coke is a combination reaction. CO₂ is not a pollutant. Then, why is combustion of coke harmful?
(ii) Which reaction followed by two combination reactions are involved in white wash of walls?
(iii) Give one use of tin plating in daily life.
(iv) How have photochemical reactions played an important role in photography?
items.answer:
(i) CO₂ is not a pollutant when present in the atmosphere up to a certain percentage. Rather, it helps to maintain the temperature of the Earth. Combustion of coke is harmful as it increases the concentration of CO₂ in the atmosphere, which causes global warming (greenhouse effect).
(ii) Reaction of calcium with oxygen gives quicklime (CaO), which combines with water to form CaCO₃.
(iii) Tiffin boxes made up of steel are either tin plated or nickel plated to protect them from rusting. However, tin-plating is preferred because tin is non-poisonous and hence does not contaminate the food kept in them.
(iv) A photographic film used in black and white photography is a celluloid film coated with silver chloride. Its working is based on the decomposition of silver chloride in the presence of sunlight.
items.ocr: OCR repair: 'CO $2$ s not a pollutant' → 'CO₂ is not a pollutant'. Source defect: the printed answer (ii) is incomplete — white washing begins with the thermal DECOMPOSITION of limestone (CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂), and the two combination reactions that follow are CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ and Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O; the printed answer skips the decomposition step and the Ca(OH)₂ intermediate. Printed answer reproduced as it stands.

items.stem:
Ferrous sulphate crystals on heating in a dry boiling tube give the following reaction:
2FeSO₄(s) --Heat--> Fe₂O₃(s) + SO₂(g) + SO₃(g)
(i) What is the colour change in this reaction?
(ii) Name the type of reaction.
(iii) Which gas has a smell of burning sulphur?
(iv) What happens when SO₂ gas is passed through water?
items.answer:
(i) The colour changes from green to brown.
(ii) The reaction is called a decomposition reaction.
(iii) Sulphur dioxide.
(iv) It forms sulphurous acid: SO₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₃ (sulphurous acid).
items.ocr: LaTeX \xrightarrow{Heat} rewritten as '--Heat-->' and subscripts converted to Unicode. items.stem:
While performing an experiment in the chemistry lab, a student took lead nitrate solution in a test tube. To this solution, he added potassium iodide solution.
(i) Write balanced chemical equation for this reaction.
(ii) What are the different names given to this reaction?
(iii) What is the colour of the precipitate formed?
(iv) Name the compound precipitated.
items.answer:
(i) Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) + 2KI(aq) → PbI₂(s) + 2KNO₃(aq)
(ii) The reaction is called a double displacement reaction as well as a precipitation reaction, as one of the products is an insoluble substance.
(iii) The colour of the precipitate is yellow.
(iv) Lead iodide.
items.ocr: The printed answer (i) is truncated in the source — it ends at the arrow, 'Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) + 2KI(aq) ⟶', with the products dropped. The products PbI₂(s) + 2KNO₃(aq) were restored from the book's own parts (iii) 'yellow precipitate' and (iv) 'lead iodide'.

items.stem:
In a redox reaction, if a substance gains oxygen, it is said to be oxidized. If a substance loses oxygen during a reaction, it is said to be reduced. In the reaction:
CuO + H₂ --Heat--> Cu + H₂O
(i) Which substance gets oxidized and which substance gets reduced?
(ii) What is the colour change in the above reaction?
(iii) What other name is given to this redox reaction?
(iv) Is this reaction, ZnO + H₂ --Heat--> Zn + H₂O, feasible? If not, then why?
items.answer:
(i) H₂ gets oxidized to H₂O and CuO gets reduced to Cu.
(ii) CuO is a black solid whereas Cu is reddish brown.
(iii) Displacement reaction.
(iv) The reaction is not possible. H₂ is less reactive than zinc, so hydrogen cannot displace zinc from zinc oxide.

items.stem:
When a metal is attacked by substances around it such as moisture, acids, etc., it is said to corrode, and this process is called corrosion. The black coating on silver, green coating on copper and reddish-brown powder on iron surface are some examples of corrosion.
(i) What is the name given to the corrosion of iron?
(ii) What is the formula of green colour coating on copper?
(iii) Name two methods to prevent corrosion of iron.
(iv) Is corrosion a redox reaction?
items.answer:
(i) Rusting.
(ii) CuCO₃·Cu(OH)₂ — basic copper carbonate.
(iii) (a) Painting of an iron object. (b) Applying oil/grease on an iron object.
(iv) Yes.

items.stem:
Magnesium ribbon burns in air with a dazzling white flame. This is due to the formation of a white solid. This white solid dissolves in water and gives a solution which turns red litmus blue.
(i) Write the equation for the reaction of magnesium ribbon in air.
(ii) Name the type of reaction.
(iii) Why does the white dazzling flame appear?
(iv) What happens when white solid is dissolved in water?
items.answer:
(i) 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
(ii) The reaction is called a combination reaction.
(iii) This is due to the formation of magnesium oxide.
(iv) MgO + H₂O → Mg(OH)₂ (white solid)
items.ocr: The printed question number was lost by OCR — this block runs straight on from the answer to item 260 and is followed by item 262, so the number 261 is inferred from position. Printed part (i) reads 'Write the equation or the reaction' — 'or' corrected to 'for'.

items.stem:
You are given the following unbalanced equation:
Fe(s) + H₂O(g) → Fe₃O₄(s) + H₂(g)
(i) Write balanced chemical equations.
(ii) Write which substance gets oxidized and which substance gets reduced.
(iii) What name can be given to this reaction other than redox reaction?
(iv) How will you test the gas evolved?
(v) Identify the oxidizing agent and reducing agent.
items.answer:
(i) 3Fe(s) + 4H₂O(g) → Fe₃O₄(s) + 4H₂(g)
(ii) Fe gets oxidized to Fe₃O₄ and H₂O gets reduced to form H₂ gas.
(iii) Displacement reaction.
(iv) H₂ gas gives a pop sound when a burning match stick is brought near the gas.
(v) Oxidizing agent: H₂O(g); Reducing agent: Fe(s).
items.ocr: The given equation printed as 'Fe(s) H₂O(g) ⟶ Fe₃O₄(s) + H₂(g)' — the '+' between the two reactants was dropped by OCR and has been restored. items.stem:
The figure shows a student heating ferrous sulphate crystals in a boiling tube over a burner and wafting the gas gently towards the nose (the labels warn: do not point the mouth of the boiling tube at your neighbours or yourself). After seeing the above image answer the following questions.
(i) What was the colour of the crystals before heating and after heating?
(ii) Write the chemical equation for the reaction.
(iii) Name the reaction.
(iv) Which pungent smelling gas is evolved during the reaction? What is the nature of this gas?
(v) Write the name of the solid substance formed.
items.answer:
(i) Before heating: pale green colour. After heating: reddish brown.
(ii) 2FeSO₄(s) --Heat--> Fe₂O₃(s) + SO₂(g) + SO₃(g)
(iii) Thermal decomposition.
(iv) The pungent smelling gas is sulphur dioxide, SO₂. It is a non-metallic oxide, hence acidic in nature.
(v) Ferric oxide or iron (III) oxide.
